A first stop before [Classic Organs Compared](organ-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the pipe organ is and when it was made.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Find records it is on.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- A **pipe organ** sounds by blowing wind through pipes; a **stop** turns on one **rank** of pipes, one pipe a key (Wikipedia, "Organ stop").
- **This page's pipe organ is not a real instrument.** It is a small made-up stop list: a Great (lower manual), a Swell (upper manual, in a box with shutters) and a Pedal.
- Combining stops is called **registration** (Wikipedia, "Organ stop").

## Its sound

- **Families**: principals (the organ's own sound), flutes, strings and reeds (Wikipedia).
- **Footage**: 8′ is the pitch of the key, 16′ an octave lower, 4′ an octave higher; 2⅔′ and 1⅗′ are *mutations*, sounding a twelfth and a seventeenth above (Wikipedia).
- A **mixture** sounds several high ranks at once, its number of ranks in Roman numerals (Wikipedia).
- **Couplers** let one keyboard play another's stops; the **Swell box** is a pedal that opens its shutters (couplers and box: general knowledge, UNVERIFIED).

## The panel

This is the pipe organ panel from [Classic Organs Compared](organ-compare.qmd), drawn after the real one (not a copy). Play it from the keys under the panel or the computer keys (a w s e d f t g y h u j k); **Keys play** picks the manual. Pull a drawbar or press a tab while you play. The sound is this site's own model; nobody has compared it with the real instrument.

## Guided tour

Each step loads a registration and plays chords on the Great, a tune on the Swell and a bass on the Pedal.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="pipe-flutes"><p><b>Quiet flutes.</b> Gedackt 8′ and Spitzflöte 4′ on the Swell, Subbass 16′ in the pedal. Listen: soft, with a little breath (chiff) as notes start.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="pipe-cornet"><p><b>A cornet.</b> Flutes at 8′, 4′, 2⅔′, 2′ and 1⅗′ together on the Swell: the mutations make one reedy solo sound from flutes.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="pipe-plenum"><p><b>Principal chorus.</b> Principal 8′, Octave 4′, Fifteenth 2′ and Mixture IV on the Great, coupled to the pedal. Listen: bright and grand.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="pipe-widor" data-set="{&quot;g_trp8&quot;:false,&quot;s_ob8&quot;:false,&quot;p_trb16&quot;:false}"><p><b>Full organ without reeds.</b> Everything coupled, but no reed stops.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="pipe-widor"><p><b>Add the reeds.</b> Trumpet, Oboe and Trombone. Listen: the sound gets a brassy edge.</p></div>
```

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>A stop marked 4′ sounds…</b></p><ul><li>An octave above the key</li><li>An octave below</li><li>At the key's pitch</li><li>Two octaves below</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia, "Organ stop".</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Which family imitates brass and reed instruments?</b></p><ul><li>Reeds</li><li>Principals</li><li>Flutes</li><li>Mixtures</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Reed stops.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Mixture IV means…</b></p><ul><li>Four ranks sound for each key</li><li>The fourth stop</li><li>Four keyboards</li><li>Four pedals</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Roman numeral = number of ranks.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Is this page&#x27;s pipe organ a real instrument?</b></p><ul><li>No: a made-up stop list</li><li>Yes: Saint-Sulpice</li><li>Yes: a Hammond</li><li>Yes: a theatre organ</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Said at the top of the page.</p></div>
```
